title: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery: in-product diagnostics for case access, security filters and holds
summary: Hold pending corrections to the existing troubleshooting controls. The case-membership path only adds users, not role groups, and the existing Help-pane diagnostic is unavailable in GCC High and DoD. The planned diagnostic checks and rollout windows otherwise match Microsoft's notice.

claims.claim: To analyse a user's data with premium eDiscovery features enabled, that user needs Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5 unless covered by the stated add-on alternative.
claims.quote: To analyze a user's data when premium eDiscovery features are enabled, the user must be assigned an Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5 license.

claims.claim: The premium-data alternative is Microsoft Purview Suite or Microsoft 365 eDiscovery and Audit for Office 365 E1 or Office 365 or Microsoft 365 E3 users.
claims.quote: Alternatively, users with an Office 365 E1 or an Office 365 or Microsoft 365 E3 license can be assigned a Microsoft Purview Suite (formerly known as Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance) or Microsoft 365 eDiscovery and Audit add-on license.

claims.claim: The permissions page does not identify the three new diagnostics as the subject of its premium licensing rule.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery diagnostics case access; eDiscovery diagnostics security filters; eDiscovery diagnostics hold distribution. Read Assign permissions in eDiscovery in full; it names the existing RBAC check but does not mention the three new checks.

claims.claim: The case-access article says users must be added to the eDiscovery Manager role group before accessing a case.
claims.quote: before a user can access an eDiscovery case (and perform tasks in the case), you must add the user to the eDiscovery Manager role group in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: The permissions article also documents eDiscovery permissions through Compliance Administrator, Organization Management and Reviewer role groups.
claims.quote: you can also assign users eDiscovery-related permissions by adding them to the Compliance Administrator, Organization Management, and Reviewer role groups.

claims.claim: For users who are not eDiscovery Administrators, visible cases are limited to cases they belong to.
claims.quote: For users who aren't eDiscovery Administrators, the cases shown are limited to those where the user is a member.

claims.claim: An eDiscovery Administrator can view and access all eDiscovery cases.
claims.quote: An eDiscovery Administrator can view and access all eDiscovery cases, they can audit and oversee all cases and associated compliance searches.

claims.claim: Search permissions filters govern the mailboxes and sites an eDiscovery manager can search.
claims.quote: Use search permissions filtering to let an eDiscovery manager search only a subset of mailboxes and sites in your organization.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Adding or removing a role in a role group removes the role group from every eDiscovery case it belongs to.
claims.quote: If you add or remove a role from a role group that you added as a member of a case, the role group is automatically removed as a member of the case (or any case the role group is a member of).

claims.claim: eDiscovery Manager membership is assigned in the Purview portal through Settings > Role groups > eDiscovery Manager > Edit > Manage eDiscovery Manager > Choose users or Choose groups.
claims.quote: Go to Settings > Role groups. On Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions, select eDiscovery Manager. Select Edit. On Manage eDiscovery Manager, select Choose users or Choose groups.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember "eDiscoveryManager" -Member <name of security group> adds a group to the eDiscovery Managers subgroup.
claims.quote:
You can add a mail-enabled security group as a member of the eDiscovery Managers subgroup ... by using the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
Add-RoleGroupMember "eDiscoveryManager" -Member <name of security group>

claims.claim: Assigning eDiscovery permissions requires Organization Management membership or the Role Management role.
claims.quote: You need to be a member of the Organization Management role group or be assigned the Role Management role to assign eDiscovery permissions in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: The Purview path eDiscovery > Cases > case > Case settings > Access and permissions > Users > Add provides the row's control for adding users and role groups to a case.
claims.quote: Under Users, select Add to add users to the case. You can also choose to add a role group to the case by selecting Add under Role groups.
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].ui.path and its rendered table path with 'eDiscovery > Cases > case > Case settings > Access and permissions > Users or Role groups > Add'. The cited page uses Users for individual users and Role groups for role groups.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/cases/ediscoveryCases/{ediscoveryCaseId}/caseMembers adds a user or role group as a case member.
claims.quote:
The ediscoveryCaseMember can be one of two types: a user or a role group.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/cases/ediscoveryCases/b0073e4e-4184-41c6-9eb7-8c8cc3e2288b/caseMembers

claims.claim: The case-member request body sets recipientType.
claims.quote: recipientType ... Specifies the recipient type of the eDiscovery case member. The possible values are: user, roleGroup, unknownFutureValue. Required.

claims.claim: The request identifies a case member by id, or by displayName for a role group or smtpAddress for a user.
claims.quote: id ... The ID of the eDiscovery case member. If not specified, then either displayName (for role group) or smtpAddress (for user) must be provided.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed how the new diagnostics read the existing underlying case-access, filter and hold controls.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery diagnostics case access; eDiscovery diagnostics security filters; eDiscovery diagnostics hold distribution. Read case-access, permissions, search-filter, hold-management and self-help diagnostic pages; no implementation mapping for the new checks.

claims.claim: An admin UI control for configuring search permissions filters is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery search permissions filtering portal UI New-ComplianceSecurityFilter Get-ComplianceSecurityFilter. Read Configure search permissions filtering in eDiscovery in full and search excerpts from its cmdlet references; configuration is documented through PowerShell, not a portal path.

claims.claim: New-ComplianceSecurityFilter -FilterName <name of filter> -Users <user or role group> -Filters <filter> creates the search permissions filter.
claims.quote:
Use the New-ComplianceSecurityFilter cmdlet to create a search permissions filter. Here's the basic syntax for this cmdlet:
New-ComplianceSecurityFilter -FilterName <name of filter> -Users <user or role group> -Filters <filter>

claims.claim: Compliance security filter cmdlets require Organization Management membership and the eDiscovery administrator role.
claims.quote: To run the compliance security filter cmdlets, you need to be a member of the Organization Management role group and have the eDiscovery administrator role assigned in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Search permissions filter cmdlets run in Security & Compliance PowerShell with connections to both it and Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: You need to connect to both Exchange Online and Security & Compliance PowerShell to use the compliance security filter cmdlets. These cmdlets require access to mailbox properties, which is why you need to connect to Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: Get-ComplianceSecurityFilter returns the existing search permissions filters.
claims.quote: Use Get-ComplianceSecurityFilter to return a list of search permissions filters. Use the FilterName parameter to return information for a specific search filter.

claims.where: controls[3].ui; Governance controls table; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Hold policies can be retried in Purview through eDiscovery > Cases > case > Hold policies > hold policy > Policy actions > Retry policy.
claims.quote: Select the eDiscovery solution card, then select Cases ... Select a case, then select the Hold policies tab ... select the hold policy you want to retry ... select Policy actions > Retry policy.

claims.claim: Set-CaseHoldPolicy -Identity <policyname> -RetryDistribution retries hold policy distribution.
claims.quote: Run the Set-CaseHoldPolicy -Identity "policyname" -RetryDistribution to resolve the issue.

claims.claim: Get-CaseHoldPolicy -Identity <policyname> -DistributionDetail reads hold distribution status separately.
claims.quote:
$status = Get-CaseHoldPolicy -Identity <policyname> -DistributionDetail
if($status.DistributionStatus -ne "Pending")

claims.where: Governance controls; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The existing eDiscovery RBAC diagnostic is presented as a Help-pane troubleshooting route without a cloud restriction.
claims.quote: Diagnostics in the Help pane aren't available in the following environments: GCC High, DoD, and Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet.
claims.fix: Add to the existing RBAC diagnostic description: 'The existing Help-pane diagnostic is unavailable in GCC High, DoD and Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet, according to Self-help diagnostics for Microsoft Purview.' Apply this qualification to its mention in Risk assessment too. Do not apply that restriction to the new checks in MC1515937.

claims.claim: The existing RBAC diagnostic is found through Purview Help > Ask a question > search for Diag:edisRBACdiag, with the permissions article abbreviating the route to Help search.
claims.quote: Select the Help icon ... In the Help and support pane, select Ask a question. In the search box, enter a brief description ... Assign permissions in eDiscovery: Select the Help control ... Enter Diag:edisRBACdiag in search.

claims.claim: The existing eDiscovery RBAC diagnostic checks Search, Export or Preview role assignments for a designated account.
claims.quote: Checks eDiscovery role-based access control (RBAC) to determine whether the Search, Export, or Preview roles are assigned to the designated administrator account.

claims.claim: MC1515937 does not mention end users or case reviewers as affected groups.
claims.quote:

- eDiscovery admins.
